texts.facts: The complainant took the sample of chilly powder and sent the same for analysis and in report, found the chilly powder to be adulterated and accordingly, the accused having found committing the breach of the provisions of Sections 7 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (the said Act) and rules framed thereunder, committed the offence punishable under Section 16 of the said Act, and hence, a complaint came be to registered against them. 2.1 Upon complaint being filed and pursuant to the summons issued, the respondent - accused appeared before the Court. Since the accused did not plead guilty, trial was proceeded against the accused. Being aggrieved by the same, the State has preferred the present appeal.

It is submitted that the impugned judgment of the trial Court is based on presumptions and inferences and thereby, it is against the facts and the evidence on record.
